evidence: "m = n − 1" and "deploying all m conduits would successfully connect all n modules"; DeepSeek uses "Prune non-critical leaves"; GPT-OSS uses "iterative DFS to get parent order"
affordance_in_statement: m = n − 1. The system architecture guarantees that deploying all m conduits would successfully connect all n modules into a single network.
removal_suggestion: This affordance cannot be removed without changing the immutable edge count or the connectivity promise: a connected undirected graph with n−1 edges is necessarily a tree. If changing mutable task semantics is permitted, remove the connectivity guarantee and explicitly define an output for disconnected instances; otherwise there is no valid rewording that removes this structural shortcut.

common_affordance: The graph is a connected undirected graph with exactly n−1 edges, so it is a tree and has a unique path between every pair of modules.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: The solution applies generic Kruskal processing, sorting all edges by weight, rather than directly identifying the unique tree subtree connecting the critical processors; this can select or account for edges according to MST logic instead of the required terminal subtree.

The solution starts Prim's algorithm from a critical node, treating the task like a minimum spanning-tree or terminal-expansion problem instead of exploiting the fixed tree and excluding irrelevant branches.

recommended_edit: There is no edit that defeats all surviving solutions while preserving the immutable constraints: the values m = n−1 and connectedness intrinsically force a tree. If a task change is allowed, replace the connectivity guarantee with general graphs, define an explicit result for disconnected cases, and retain the same integer output format.
regression_risk: Removing or weakening the connectivity guarantee could make the already-defeated Kruskal and Prim solutions pass on instances where the intended task becomes a conventional MST or disconnected-graph problem.
